title: Past conversations — sign-off
lead: Everything below is real, captured from the design sandbox with fake data — no back end exists yet. Most steps just ask “does this look right?” — Yes or No. Three are decisions with options to pick from: how much opens by itself when Claude searches, whether the “Referenced conversations” list stays, and how Claude hands you a conversation.

steps.path: Chat → Claude searches your past conversations
steps.headline: When Claude searches, how much should be open already?

options.label: Leave both shut
options.summary: The group of tools is shut, and the results card inside it is shut too.
options.cost: Your chat stays quiet, but opening a conversation always takes two clicks.

options.label: Open the results
options.summary: One click on the group and the conversations are already there.
options.cost: Nothing moves until you ask, and the card is ready when you do.

options.label: Open both
options.summary: The conversations are on screen the moment the search finishes.
options.cost: Pushes the rest of your chat down every time Claude searches, even when you only wanted the answer.

highlight.selector: js:document.querySelector("[title='Read this conversation in the side pane']")?.closest('li')

steps.headline: One result row: title on top, project, date and tags underneath, two buttons at the right.
steps.changed: Every found conversation becomes a row you can act on.
steps.notice: Preview and Resume sit in the same place on every row, so your eye never hunts for them.

steps.headline: Eight situations one search can return, shown together in the design sandbox.
steps.changed: Found and openable, blocked two different ways, gone from this device, a conversation from the other assistant, no title, unreadable, and simply not found.
steps.notice: Every case has a row — none of them silently disappears from the list.

highlight.text: Not synced to this device yet

steps.headline: When Resume cannot work, the row says why in words, where the date would normally sit.
steps.changed: The reason replaces the date instead of hiding inside a hover tooltip.
steps.notice: You can tell at a glance why a button is greyed out, without pointing at it.

steps.headline: A conversation whose saved text is gone from this device greys out Preview as well as Resume.
steps.changed: Both buttons switch off together when there is nothing left to read.
steps.notice: The row still appears, so you know the conversation existed rather than wondering why it vanished.

steps.headline: If Claude trims the search output itself, the answer stays plain text instead of becoming a card.
steps.changed: A shortened result is shown exactly as it came back.
steps.notice: No buttons on a trimmed result — building a card from half an answer could point you at the wrong conversation.

steps.headline: Opening one named conversation shows a single row under the heading “Past conversation”.
steps.changed: Searching and opening one conversation get their own headings.
steps.notice: One row, same two buttons — nothing else changes between the two shapes.

steps.surface: Side panel · reading a past conversation
steps.headline: The reading panel's top bar: list, title, Resume, tag, expand, close.
steps.changed: Resume is a labelled button in the bar, the way file views carry their buttons.
steps.notice: Resume opens the conversation as a new tab in this window — not a separate window.

steps.surface: Side panel · reading a past conversation
steps.headline: Where Claude used tools between messages, the panel marks the gap instead of hiding it.
steps.changed: A quiet line counts what is not shown, for example “3 tool calls not shown”.
steps.notice: The conversation never looks like it flowed straight through when it did not.

steps.surface: Side panel · scrolled to the top
steps.headline: A caption at the top says this is a past conversation, read-only, and which assistant it came from.
steps.changed: The panel names what you are looking at rather than looking like a live chat.
steps.notice: You cannot type into it; the caption says so before you try.

steps.surface: Side panel · scrolled to the top
steps.headline: Only the most recent stretch loads; “Load older” fetches the previous stretch on demand.
steps.changed: The panel pages backwards instead of loading a whole long conversation at once.
steps.notice: Long conversations open immediately; older parts arrive when you ask for them.

steps.headline: The tag icon opens the same tag-and-note editor the resume screen already uses.
steps.changed: Nothing new was drawn — the existing editor was reused as-is.
steps.notice: Tags and notes you add here are the same ones the resume screen shows.

steps.headline: Right-clicking inside a past conversation offers the same menu the live chat does.
steps.changed: Ask about this, Copy and Select all now work inside a previewed conversation.
steps.notice: Nothing extra and nothing missing compared with right-clicking your current chat.

steps.path: Preview two conversations → open the list
steps.headline: Keep the running list of conversations you have opened, or cut it?

options.label: Keep it
options.summary: Every past conversation you open this session collects under the file list.
options.cost: Costs a slice of a list you already scroll, and titles are cut to about one word at that width.

options.label: Cut it
options.summary: The list goes away; the search cards stay in your chat, which is how you got there anyway.
options.cost: Nothing to lose — it comes out cleanly, and the reading panel does not depend on it.

steps.path: Preview a conversation whose saved text cannot be opened
steps.headline: When a conversation cannot be read, the panel shows the real reason and a Retry button.
steps.changed: The underlying failure is repeated word for word instead of being replaced by a guess.
steps.notice: The text can look technical, because it is the machine's own words — but it is never invented.

steps.headline: At phone width Resume shrinks to an arrow so the whole bar still fits.
steps.changed: The bar keeps all six controls at 390 across instead of dropping any.
steps.notice: Nothing wraps or gets cut off, but Resume loses its word at this width.

steps.headline: The look is settled. How should Claude actually hand you a conversation?

options.label: Reuse a command
options.summary: Treat one of its existing commands as the signal to draw this card.
options.cost: Smallest change and works today, but it borrows a command meant for something else, so it can fire when you did not want it.

options.label: New plugin command
options.summary: A command that means exactly this, and nothing else.
options.cost: Cleanest meaning, but anyone who already installed the plugin will not receive it until a separate fix ships.

options.label: Build it for YouCoded
options.summary: Build it properly for the assistant that lives in this app.
options.cost: Small and contained, but it works only for that assistant — never for Claude Code.
